label: 360 degree asset detail
description: The page every item opens into: a full-width identity header, a tab bar across the object's facets, and a two-column body whose columns scroll independently. The left column holds the authored narrative (policy, glossary links, description, relations); the right column holds a completion meter over a second tab set (Properties, People, Suggestions) that is itself the densest form in the product. Derived from a Studio Dataset page.
when: Use for any single item that has more facets than one screen can hold, where the facets are peers rather than steps. Do NOT use faceted-browse: this composes one object, not a collection. Do NOT use search-filtered-table for the whole page; that shape is real here but it is the content of ONE tab (Fields), not the page. The distinguishing trait is two independent tab levels plus two independently scrolling columns, so the tab bar and header stay fixed while either column moves. Observed in Studio; the pattern also claims Explorer, which this capture did not check.

slots.header: Breadcrumb, then the identity row (item type tag, Shared tag, title, lifecycle stage tag, Actions button) over three metadata lines: technical name, a catalog / data product / connection path with links, and a last-updated date.
slots.tabs: The item's facets (eight on a Dataset), some carrying a count, one greyed when the source supplies nothing. Opposite them, two avatar stacks: curators and contacts, which are a summary of the People panel.
slots.left: Authored narrative: access-request policy select, glossary multi-select of removable chips, a description block (use-source checkbox, summary, full rich-text description), and a relations section that is empty far more often than not.
slots.right: Completion meter, then a second tab set. Properties is a long form in the item type's groups (DATA Contract, OUTPUT PORT, Cataloging, GOVERNANCE) mixing selects, multi-selects, text and date fields, ending in a read-only source-properties list.
slots.right-people: Not drawn here. Two role sections (Curator, Contact), each with an add-person icon action and a two-column grid of avatar, name and a remove control.
slots.right-suggestions: Not drawn here. A four-way segmented control (Accepted, Rejected, Pending, All) over suggestion cards: author avatar, name, relative time, status at the right, body text, a comment textarea, and a Reject/Accept footer pair.
slots.toast: Not drawn here. A transient error toast appears bottom-centre on a slow response. It is real chrome on this page, and the DS tier has no toast component to carry it.

renderNotes: Inside a VERTICAL frame, never set `sizing.horizontal:"FILL"`. `render-node.js` emits `flex:1` for it with no axis awareness, so in a column it distributes HEIGHT; width already fills because the renderer only sets `align-items` when `counterAxisAlignItems` is given, so the flex default of `stretch` applies. FILL is correct only for children of a HORIZONTAL frame, which is why the two body columns carry it and nothing below them does. Plugin #298.

Every value is the captured Dataset's (COUNT BY ORDER STATUS, manufacturing.zeenea.app, 2026-09-30). The three sections are shared parts; this page gives them its values through each SECTION node's `values`.
The full description is the product's rich text: a heading, a paragraph, a schema table (drawn with `table`) and a bullet list of key characteristics, cut here after the table.

The empty relations block is `empty-state` with Headline "No related Datasets" and Body, Cta and Secondary set to "": the product draws a folder illustration over those words, with no body and no buttons. The renderer draws the same illustration at every Size, so Size=Small, chosen for a block inside a column, does not change the render.
`tabs` has no count badge, so a count is written into the label text ("Fields 2").
`checkbox` carries its own label here ("Use source description"); the product has no "Switch to rich text" control on this page any more.
